text:
Ilya Protas has become the example in a hard Capitals month. On Nov. 24, RMNB reported that Spencer Carbery singled out the 20-year-old as the model for a struggling team to follow, and his ice time says the coach means it: 17 minutes or more in two of his last four games, after single digits earlier in November.

He's a 6'6" third-round pick who scored 124 points in his last OHL season with Windsor, and the passing has carried over. Nine points in 22 games, four on the power play, and seven of them assists. The underlying play is the selling point: Washington gets 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (chance quality) with him on, better than without him, and his team has finished about four goals below its chances around him, which has cost him points.

Twenty-two games at 12 minutes a night is a small sample, so read the rates loosely. Our range for his season runs from 27 to 48 points, wide because the role is still moving. Watch whether the bigger minutes stick.
